`CoherentInverse` adds coherent componentwise inversion to the existing
DiamondsAndVStacks D0.25 component equivalences; it does not restate them. For
f:V→U, the mate is G(f)β_V→β_Uη_UG(f)β_V→β_UF(f)η_Vβ_V→β_UF(f).
The first and last arrows use the inverse counit at U and unit at V. Comparison
with chosen component units/counits is through the equality-induced isomorphism,
not an arbitrary existential arrow that could absorb a wrong normalization.

## Mathematical pass: interpretation

Each row identifies a statement, its applicable instances and the outcome/change.
The README rows include their own API and Check statements; the crosswalk keeps
all packet statements, including those routed to existing owners. The native
rows record inspection of the full elaborated type, including inherited
`variable`/`include` hypotheses, and link the exact source declaration.

“Pass at the stated scope” means the mathematical construction, equation and
applicable degenerate/negative cases were checked with the hypotheses shown. It
does not mean a `sorry` was proved. The case suites below collect the common
fixtures; each row names its specific checks when present. An excluded case
tests the need for a hypothesis rather than claiming a theorem outside it.

| Suite | Instances and computed controls |
|---|---|
| P: projective parameters | P(0)=∅, P(L)=S and O(1)=L; Gr₀(E)=S, Gr₁(0)=∅; Gr₁(O/(t))=V(t) is not smooth; a free submodule A(t,0)⊂A² has nonfree quotient; Plücker minors (1,c,d,−a,−b,ad−bc) also satisfy the equation in characteristic 2; P⁰ has H⁰(O(−7))=A, P¹ has H¹(O(−2))=A and H¹(O(−1))=0; det(O(1)⊕O) gives top direct image O(−1). |
| H: Hilbert/regularity/bounds | Zero sheaf gives zero polynomial; dual-number point gives length 2; weight-two grading is excluded; three collinear/noncollinear points have the same polynomial 3 and different ideal regularity 3/2; m<a cannot generate the shifted presentation; rank-zero Quot is valid; dimension-zero and curve numerical cases are separate. |
| D: effective descent/restriction | Identity descent recovers the module; faithfully flat extensions descend objects and maps; Z→F₂ sends multiplication by 2 to zero, so nonflat pullback is not exact; empty finite source gives a terminal Hom and two disjoint source points give a product; restriction uses actual associators and a faithful-flat comparison, not arbitrary base change. |
| G: gerbes/bands | Trivial band; connected BC₃ has 3 sections, discrete two-component C₃ has 9, empty connected fixture has the trivial section group; BS₃ has centre of cardinality 1 and a noncentral transposition fails surjectivity; C₄→C₂ sends 1→1 and 2→0; a band-changing coefficient is rejected without assuming band preservation; root O(1) on P¹ is nonneutral and O(2) has root O(1). |
| F: affine/profinite | Trivial/identity/surjective affine groups; arbitrary infinite-type Hopf algebra; finite étale image subgroup; simultaneous two-stage objects and arrows; unique 2-cells versus the ordinary idempotent monoid {1,0}; no implicit finite-presentation quotient theorem. |
| R: rigidification | BC₄→BC₂ kills a kernel of order 2 but leaves inertia 2; level 2 allows −1, level ≥3 needs polarization and invertibility; the unpolarized shear on E² fixes N-torsion; μ_p is not étale; a node admits different normalization branches unless generic points are controlled. |
| A: space Picard/Artin/formal | Identity family and P¹ have scalar automorphisms under universal functions; two disjoint points have (k×)²; a sheaf class need not have a global line representative; perfect pushforward requires target-flatness and proper support; at A=k the framed BG automorphism kernel is trivial, at a small extension it can be nontrivial; x²=ε has no dual-number root in the tame coarse example; a padded smooth chart is versal but not a hull; complete and henselian G-ring approximation differ from Q[t]_(t), where sqrt(1+t) is not rational. |
| X: resolution | Unit ideal has order 0, zero ideal infinite order; (x²) has order 2 despite smooth reduced support; dual-number m² has infinite order; regularity is needed for cosupport powers; cusp residual 3/2 is cleared by the mark bound 2; weights 3/5,3/5 have pivot 1/5 after monomial blowup; terminal 0 and ∞ are distinct; old/new boundary birth blocks are kept; non-quasi-compact input need not have a finite global sequence. |
| C: analytic quotients | Dimension zero and empty boundary; z↦z² has zero derivative and is excluded from local inversion; a dual-number model keeps nilpotents; the doubled origin is locally separated but non-Hausdorff; completed algebraic/analytic stalks agree without identifying the rings; annulus localization respects radii; group order is not inverted for invariant affinoids; topological isotropy need not contradict geometric freeness. |
| V: log/vanishing/numerical | d²=0 and first-factor residue res_x(dlog x∧α)=α; moving the residue factor gives (−1)^(a−1), which agrees in characteristic 2; i! is invertible only for i<p; cyclic eigensummands use floor(iD/N), adjoint vanishing uses ceil(A); unit multiplier ideal is O and principal exponent is floor(ca); positive volume v makes intersection denominators legal; λ₀ is replaced by a positive dimension-zero bound; on a curve mv≥w+3 separates points and tangent directions. |

Suppose for every S-algebra A mapping into an affine open, every x and every countable family (M_i) of A-modules the map T_x(∏M_i)→∏T_x(M_i) is an isomorphism and O_x(∏M_i)→∏O_x(M_i) is injective. | <code>A0-extension/picard-zero-criterion</code>; <code>picard_zero_criterion</code> [L7366](../packages/AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry/README.md#L7366) | Suite A. The space Picard sheaf is represented locally finitely presented under the representability hypotheses stated here. The base is Noetherian and reduced, and the identity component of each geometric fibre is smooth of a locally constant dimension. The étale component and neutral-open construction of §7.8 supplies the algebraic-space extension. Smooth fibres alone over a nonreduced base are insufficient. Assume B is locally Noetherian and P is the relative Picard algebraic space above. In the scheme-represented case, if the identity components P_s⁰ are smooth of locally constant dimension, Pic⁰ is an open finite-type group subscheme; it is smooth when B is reduced, and proper and closed in P when all P_s⁰ are proper and P is separated. For algebraic spaces, under the requested neutral-component extension, the same conclusions hold. Over a nonreduced B instead require formal smoothness of P along the neutral component; local finite presentation then yields smoothness. With proper geometric identity components and separated P the resulting Pic⁰ is a smooth proper finitely presented group space. | Pass at stated scope; closing block: <code>picard_zero_criterion</code> |

The image of a relative class has zero obstruction exactly when it is represented by a line bundle on X. With a section the obstruction vanishes and the sequence recovers the prior split Picard comparison. | Pass at stated scope; closing block: <code>picard_brauer_obstruction</code> |

Let f:X→B be proper flat finitely presented with universal functions, M a finite locally free commutative group scheme over B and D(M) its Cartier dual. There is a natural isomorphism of fppf sheaves R¹f_*(D(M)_X)≅Hom_B(M,Pic_{X/B}). Thus a homomorphism into the Picard sheaf gives fppf-locally on B a D(M)-torsor on X. With a section, rigidifying the torsor along it gives the pointed global correspondence. | <code>A0-extension/raynaud-degree-one</code>; <code>raynaud_degree_one_cohomologicallyFlat</code> [L7412](../packages/AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry/README.md#L7412) | Suite A. A generic degree-one divisor without N* does not meet the theorem.; The section conclusion uses the curve Picard formal-smoothness route; an arbitrary section is not asserted to be a Cartier divisor at a singular point. Let f:X→S be a proper flat finitely presented relative curve over a discrete valuation trait satisfying N*. | <code>A0-extension/space-analytification</code>; <code>SpaceAnalytification</code> [L7424](../packages/AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry/README.md#L7424) | Suite A. Complex scheme analytification is constructed in §7.10.1; AdicSpacesPartII supplies rigid scheme analytification. In the nonarchimedean case existence is not assumed for every locally separated X. For a complex algebraic space X locally of finite type with locally separated diagonal, take an étale scheme presentation R⇉U and construct X^an as the analytic quotient of R^an⇉U^an. The local-isomorphism relation glues analytic structure, including nilpotents. Over a complete nontrivially valued nonarchimedean field K use an existing quotient of this analytified relation; separated X has such a quotient by the next theorem. | <code>A0-extension/separated-nonarch-analytification</code>; <code>separated_nonarch_analytification</code> [L7440](../packages/AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry/README.md#L7440) | Suite C. Separatedness, not merely local separatedness, guarantees existence. AdicSpacesPartII supplies the rigid scheme substrate; §7.10.2 builds the additional Berkovich/graded-germ quotient substrate; this target is their separated finite-type space extension by the same étale-relation quotient construction. Every separated algebraic space locally of finite type over a complete nontrivially valued nonarchimedean field admits rigid analytification, compatible with the scheme construction. On the Berkovich side an étale equivalence relation R⇉U with closed-immersion diagonal has a separated analytic quotient; good and strictly analytic properties descend. | Pass at stated scope; closing block: <code>separated_nonarch_analytification</code> |
| <code>A0-extension/analytification-descent</code>; <code>analytification_descent</code> [L7450](../packages/AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry/README.md#L7450) | Suite A. In the nonarchimedean case étale morphisms stay étale and need not be local isomorphisms for the rigid topology. For analytifiable algebraic spaces, the quotient analytification is independent up to unique canonical isomorphism of the chosen étale presentation. It is functorial in morphisms and compatible with fibre products whenever the terms are analytifiable. The scheme comparison respects these identifications; complex étale morphisms yield local analytic isomorphisms. | Pass at stated scope; closing block: <code>analytification_descent</code> |
| <code>A0-extension/complex-local-comparison</code>; <code>complex_local_comparison</code> [L7460](../packages/AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry/README.md#L7460) | Suite A. Use finite-type complex objects, retain nonreduced analytic structure and respect the chosen complex points. The particular formal automorphism need not itself analytify. For finite-type complex schemes at complex points, isomorphic analytic germs imply isomorphic completed local C-algebras and hence a common pointed étale neighbourhood with residue-field isomorphisms. Conversely a common pointed étale neighbourhood yields an isomorphism of analytic germs. These conclusions extend to locally separated finite-type complex algebraic spaces by choosing étale charts and descending the local analytic identifications. | Pass at stated scope; closing block: <code>complex_local_comparison</code> |
| <code>A0-extension/proper-space-gaga</code>; <code>proper_space_gaga</code> [L7470](../packages/AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry/README.md#L7470) | Suite A. Complex coherent GAGA is a downstream C3 target, not an imported prerequisite here. For a proper morphism h:X→Y of analytifiable finite-type algebraic spaces over K and coherent F, (R^j h_*F)^an→R^j h^an_*F^an is an isomorphism for every j≥0. For X proper over K, analytification induces an exact tensor equivalence of coherent-module categories. | Pass at stated scope; closing block: <code>proper_space_gaga</code> |

For a field k, a reduced finite-type k-algebra A and a finite extension E of its total fraction ring, its relative normalization is finite by the SF.0 Nagata theorem. For A=k[t₁,…,t_d] and a finite separable extension E/k(t₁,…,t_d), the finite normalization is generically étale. Let V be a valuation subring of F, W a valuation subring of an extension field N with W∩F=V, and p∈F[T] monic. If p splits in N and every root, including its multiplicity, belongs to W, then every coefficient of p lies in V. In particular, let E/F be finite, x∈E and N/F a finite normal extension containing every conjugate of x. Let V be a valuation subring of F and W a prolongation to N. Commutative rings R,S in one fixed universe and an arbitrary ring homomorphism f:R→S; N is an arbitrary S-module. No faithful-flatness, finite-generation or Noetherian assumption. Let L=extendScalars f, U=restrictScalars f and G=(extendRestrictScalarsAdj f).toComonad. Its endofunctor is U⋙L, so G(N)=S⊗R N with S acting on the first factor. Its counit is εN(s⊗n)=s·n; its comultiplication is ΔN(s⊗n)=s⊗1⊗n, with G²(N)=S⊗R(S⊗R N). Thus an existing Comonad.Coalgebra G is exactly an S-linear d:N→S⊗R N with εN∘d=id and (idS⊗d)∘d=ΔN∘d; its existing morphisms are S-linear h with (idS⊗h)∘d=d′∘h. No new coalgebra or comonad carrier is constructed. | Pass at stated scope; <code>ModuleDescentBridge.tensor_comonad_coordinates</code> [L559](../packages/AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry/Suggested.lean#L559) |

| <code>R09.1/chow-parameters</code>; <code>chowParameters</code> [L422](../packages/AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry/README.md#L422) | Suite H. Algebraically closed characteristic-zero field for this Chow construction and the reduced generic-fibre arguments used below. A pure cycle is a finite sum Σ a_i[Z_i] with a_i>0, dim Z_i=r; degree is Σa_i deg Z_i. Native AlgebraicCycle with natural coefficients stores the multiplicities at generic points. For an algebraically closed field k of characteristic zero, integers 0≤r≤n and D≥1, construct the projective Chow coefficient scheme Ch_(r,D)(Pⁿ_k), using the reduced closed locus of multihomogeneous associated forms of degree D in each of r+1 hyperplane blocks. Its k-points are in bijection with effective pure r-cycles of degree D, with multiplicities; their Chow forms are unique up to scalar. Degree 0 is a single zero-cycle parameter. There is a closed universal support in Ch×Pⁿ whose geometric fibre has exactly the support of the corresponding cycle, as a set. Cycles supported in a fixed closed Y⊂Pⁿ give a closed coefficient locus. This construction does not assert a flat family of subschemes or representation of the cycle functor over arbitrary nonreduced bases. | Pass at stated scope; closing block: <code>chowParameters</code> |

More generally Grothendieck Lemma 2.4 gives this finiteness for reduced equidimensional geometric-fibre subschemes of a fixed projective Noetherian family with a fixed relatively very ample embedding. Reducedness and purity are part of the assertion; the Chow cycle does not record arbitrary embedded structure. | Pass at stated scope; closing block: <code>boundedDegreeHilbertPolynomials</code> |

This means at least one component meets Y; it differs from requiring every component to avoid the boundary. ### Reproducible fifteen-locator sample

A fresh seeded sample (seed 8070) was drawn from the source-backed projective, resolution, gerbe and space-Picard contracts. Their statement/hypothesis passages and the relevant supplied proof steps were re-opened after the mathematical audit. This supplements, rather than relabels, the earlier reviewer’s seed-8027 sample.

| Target | Primary-source locator | Check and scope outcome |
|---|---|---|
| <code>R09.1/numerical-very-ampleness</code> | <code>EV</code> Corollary 5.12(c), pp. 48–52; Theorem 10.16, pp. 114–116; Corollary 10.23, p. 124 | EV 5.12 is a Corollary, not a Theorem; corrected that label. Fractional SNC support, characteristic zero, i<p and the W₂ lifting hypotheses are explicit; no uniform theorem is inferred without the numerical chain. |
| <code>R09.7/local-isomorphism-resolution</code> | <code>BM1997</code> Remarks 13.1, p. 296; Theorem 13.2 and proof, pp. 297–298 | Open-isomorphism compatibility is exactly the cited theorem; the étale/local-isomorphism extension uses the separately stated normalized-presentation construction. |
| <code>A0-extension/picard-separation</code> | <code>moduli</code> Lemmas 108.9.2–108.9.4, pp. 14–15 | Proper flat finite presentation and universal functions are inherited in §108.9; separation additionally needs geometrically integral fibres. |
| <code>R09.7/controlled-transform</code> | <code>BM1997</code> Proposition 3.13 and Remark 3.14, p. 237; 4.4(i)–4.5, p. 242; Lemma 5.1, p. 248 | Strict transform is exceptional saturation; controlled transform divides by the marked power. They are not silently identified. |
| <code>R09.1/ample-powers-and-fixed-twists</code> | <code>SC</code> §13, Lemma 13.6, p.29 | Segre sections are XiYj and generate the tensor product; global generation and finite systems are supplied before using them. |
| <code>R09.7/residual-presentation</code> | <code>BM1997</code> Construction 4.23, p. 247; Proposition 4.24 andproof pp. 248,253–254 | The residual construction retains the extra monomial guard when residual value is below one; the actual transformation proof was checked. |
| <code>R09.4/locally-full-relative</code> | <code>BV19</code> Proposition3.10(2)⇔(3), Remark3.7 | Local fullness is Isom-sheaf surjectivity and the relative-gerbe property, not faithfulness. |
